body.statement: For every retained rooted C-forest \(F\) in the fixed-nuisance binary-sink slice, exactly one rational row-space alternative holds. If \(b_{\eta,t,F}^{\mathsf T}\in\operatorname{row}(A_{\eta,t,F})\), rational elimination returns \(\lambda\) with \(b_{\eta,t,F}^{\mathsf T}=\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_{\eta,t,F}\), and the forest is structurally rejected. Otherwise \(\texttt{def:canonical-forest-kernel}\) returns a nonzero \(h_{t,F}\) supported on \(J_{t,F}\) such that \(A_{\eta,t,F}h_{t,F}=0\) and \(b_{\eta,t,F}^{\mathsf T}h_{t,F}>0\).
body.justification: The lemma makes the forest load-bearing by restricting the tested columns, while row-space membership rejects forests neutralized by shared reference contexts.
body.gap: Classical hedge constructions do not impose CSI quotient sharing, and generic null-space tests do not tie the perturbation support to a retained forest trace.
body.consumer: The result gives \(Y_0\) a deterministic forest-to-perturbation compiler or a structural rejection record.
